beliefs: The box shifts each character forward by 8 codepoints, applied independently per character [E1, E2, E3, E6, E8]
The shift applies uniformly across ASCII, Latin-1, and multi-byte ranges including surrogates and near U+10FFFF [E6, E8]
A character 't' (0x74) is deleted (maps to empty string) rather than shifted [E13]
A character '|' (0x7C) maps to '(' (0x28) when it is the first character or immediately follows a space; otherwise it shifts to 0x84 [E12, E13]
All other characters including '~' (0x7E -> 0x86) follow the uniform +8 rule [E7, E9, E10, E11]
notes: E13 shows 't' maps to empty (deletion), not '('; the earlier 't'->'(' was actually the '|'-after-space rule misfiring. E12 shows '|' maps to '(' when at start or after a space, else +8. Combined with 't' deletion, this explains E4's long-string mismatches.
